legend: In the myxoid pattern, plump myofibroblasts are set in an oedematous background with blood vessels and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate rich in lymphocytes and plasma cells.

diagnosis: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour of the tongue
legend: Lesional cells are arranged in fascicles in the hypercellular pattern. This example shows limited chronic inflammation, and the tumour cells infiltrate skeletal muscle. This tumour harboured a CARS1 (CARS)::ALK fusion gene.
Collagenous stroma predominates in the hypocellular pattern, with a relatively limited proliferation of elongated spindle cells and associated chronic inflammatory cells.

diagnosis: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour of the oral mucosa
legend: The spindle-shaped myofibroblasts have oval nuclei and vesicular chromatin with small, prominent nucleoli; scattered intranuclear pseudoinclusions can be seen.

diagnosis: Hypopharyngeal inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour after crizotinib therapy
legend: A large inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour of the hypopharynx is grossly lobulated, tan, and fleshy, with areas of necrosis (yellow, left), after neoadjuvant treatment with crizotinib. This tumour harboured a ROS1 gene rearrangement, an unusual feature for head and neck inflammatory myofibroblastic tumours.
The submucosal myofibroblastic spindle cell proliferation is diffusely and strongly positive for ALK by immunohistochemistry. This tumour harboured a TIMP3::ALK rearrangement.
The polypoid tumour demonstrates a submucosal fascicular proliferation of spindle cells with admixed inflammatory cells.
The myxoid pattern shows a storiform to fascicular proliferation of spindled to plump myofibroblasts in an oedematous, loose background of lymphocytes and plasma cells.
